questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Kiran’s teacher was __doubtful on__ her success.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. "doubtful of". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "doubtful on" is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• The correct preposition to use with "doubtful" when expressing uncertainty about a particular outcome or situation is "of."
 
• **"Doubtful of" **is a standard English phrase used to express skepticism or lack of conviction about something.

Therefore, the correct sentence is -*Kiran’s teacher was **doubtful of*__* her success.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to improve it. If no improvement is required, select ‘No improvement required’.

Tomorrow, they __will be take a flight__ to their dream vacation destination.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The structure "**will be taking**" correctly represents the future continuous tense which is needed here to indicate an action that will be happening in the future.
 
• The given sentence uses "**be take**" which is grammatically incorrect, as it lacks the **continuous aspect required here**.
 
• Options "**be taking a flight**" and "**will taking a flight**" are also incorrect due to improper grammatical structure.

Hence, the correct statement is '***Tomorrow, they will be taking a flight to their dream vacation destination*.'****

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **future continuous tense** is used to talk about actions that will be happening at a particular moment in the future.

 
 
• **Example:** *I will be watching** the game at 8 PM tomorrow.*
 
 
 
• The construction of **future continuous tense** is: **will be + verb(-ing)**.
 
 
• **Example:** *She **will be meeting** us there.*

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'since years' is incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be 'for years' to indicate a **duration of time.**
 
• The correct form of the sentence should use the past participle 'painted' along with the correct preposition 'for'.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase is 'have not been painted for years'.

Hence, the correct statement is '*It seems that these walls have not been painted** for** years*.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Example with 'since': *I have lived here **since 2010***.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.

options.text: In an big city like Mumbai, we see lot of rubbish being thrown from households and factories.
In big city like Mumbai, we see a lot of rubbish being thrown from households and factories.
In a big city like Mumbai, we see a lot of rubbish being thrown from households and factories.
In a big city like Mumbai, we see an lot of rubbish being thrown from households and factories.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**In a big city like Mumbai, we see a lot of rubbish being thrown from households and factories"****.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Here we will see the sentence formation:

__
 
• Indefinite article **‘A’ **is used at the start of a consonant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let's learn more about indefinite articles:

__
 
• There are two articles in the English language:*** ‘A’ and ‘An.’***
 
• Indefinite article* **‘A’** *is used at the start of a*** consonant***, and** *‘An’*** is used at the beginning of every*** vowel. ‘An’*** is used when you use a word starting with** *vowels*, **which are** *a, e, i, o, u.***
 
 
• ***​Eg. __***__An __Owl Stays Awake in the Night.
 
• **Eg. ** __A __Girl was Walking Down the Street When She Saw a Man Following her.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Lily __has dedicate__ her life towards becoming a doctor.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **has dedicated**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **present perfect tense**.
 
• The present perfect tense is formed with **"has"** or **"have"** followed by the **past participle** of the **verb**. 
 
 
• **For example:** Vinay **has moved** into a new apartment.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in the given question, after **'has'**, the **past participle form of the verb **(dedicated) must be used.
 
• Hence, **'has dedicated'** is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Lily **has dedicated**__ her life towards becoming a doctor.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The rest of the options are **incorrect** because:

 
 
• **'had dedicate': **This is an attempt to form a past perfect tense ("had dedicated") but fails as it uses the base form **"dedicate"** instead of the past participle "dedicated." The correct past perfect form would be "had dedicated," but in this sentence, past perfect is not appropriate as we are talking about an action impacting the present.
 
• 
 **'is dedicate'**: This option incorrectly attempts to construct a present tense using **"is"** (a present form of "to be") with "dedicate." The correct present tense formation would involve using "is dedicating" if we wanted to depict an ongoing action; however, the intended meaning is about a commitment that spans past to present, making the present perfect tense ("has dedicated") more appropriate.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to improve it. If no improvement is required, select ‘No improvement required’.

I __would love fly__ a fighter jet one day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• In the given sentence, the phrase **"love fly**" is incorrect and needs to be corrected.
 
• The correct form should be "**love to fly" **as it correctly follows the verb pattern
 
 
• **"would love to" + base form of the verb**.
 
 
 
• The correct substitution would be "**would love to fly".**

Hence, the correct statement is :** *I would love to fly a fighter jet one day*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

The referee declared that the participant __who will score the highest points__ in the tally will take away the cash prize of Rs. 50 lakh.

options.text: who can score the highest point
who could score the highest point
who settles scores the highest point

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the future tense is incorrect.
 
• The sentence refers to a general statement about the participant scoring the*** highest points***, which should be in the ***present tense.***
 
• Therefore, the present tense form of the verb 'scores' should be used in place of the future tense '***will score'.***

Hence, the correct statement is '***The referee declared that the participant who scores the highest points__ in the tally will take away the cash prize of Rs. 50 lakh*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• When making **general statements or facts that are always true, the present tense is used.**
 
• For actions that will happen in the future, the future tense is used.
 
• Example: *The sun** rises** in the east.* (Present tense for a general truth)
 
• Example: *She will **travel** to Paris next month.* (Future tense for a planned future action)

The correct statement is 'The referee declared that the participant **who scores the highest points**__ in the tally will take away the cash prize of Rs. 50 lakh.'

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no improvement required, select ‘No improvement’.

__Scarcely__ he see his opponent than he went numb with fear.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'No sooner did' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'Scarcely he see' is incorrect.
 
• The correct expression is **'No sooner did he see'** as it follows the correct grammatical structure for such sentences.
 
• The structure for such sentences is: **No sooner + did + subject + base form of the verb + than**.
 
 
• **Example:** ***No sooner did** she **arrive** **than** it started raining*.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'No sooner did he see'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *No sooner did he see his opponent than he went numb with fear*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phrases **'No sooner... than'** and **'Hardly... when'** are often used to indicate that one action quickly followed another.

 
 
• **Example:** ***Hardly had** he **arrived** **when** the meeting started*.
 
 
 
• These phrases are used with the past perfect or simple past tense, and the auxiliary verb (did/had) is used before the subject.
